Looking at this problem, I need to determine the minimum number of repetitions (repeated ordered pairs) when superimposing two different Latin squares of the same order.

## Proof

**Claim:** The minimum number of repetitions possible is **0**.

**Definition.** When two Latin squares $L_1$ and $L_2$ of order $n$ are superimposed, each cell $(i,j)$ yields an ordered pair $(L_1[i,j],\, L_2[i,j])$. A *repetition* occurs when the same ordered pair appears in more than one cell. The number of repetitions is $\sum_{p} (\text{count}(p) - 1)$ over all ordered pairs $p$ with $\text{count}(p) \geq 1$, equivalently $n^2 - |\{(L_1[i,j], L_2[i,j]) : 1 \le i,j \le n\}|$.

**Construction.** We exhibit two different Latin squares of order 3 whose superposition produces no repetitions.

Let:
$$L_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad L_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

**Verification that both are Latin squares:**

- $L_1$: Every row is a permutation of $\{1,2,3\}$; every column is a permutation of $\{1,2,3\}$. ✓
- $L_2$: Every row is a permutation of $\{1,2,3\}$; every column is a permutation of $\{1,2,3\}$. ✓

**Verification that $L_1 \neq L_2$:** They differ at positions $(2,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,1)$, $(3,2)$, $(3,3)$. ✓

**Superposition** (forming ordered pairs $(L_1[i,j], L_2[i,j])$):

$$\begin{pmatrix} (1,1) & (2,2) & (3,3) \\ (2,3) & (3,1) & (1,2) \\ (3,2) & (1,3) & (2,1) \end{pmatrix}$$

The nine ordered pairs are:
$$(1,1),\; (2,2),\; (3,3),\; (2,3),\; (3,1),\; (1,2),\; (3,2),\; (1,3),\; (2,1)$$

These are all $3 \times 3 = 9$ possible ordered pairs from $\{1,2,3\} \times \{1,2,3\}$, each appearing **exactly once**. Therefore the number of repetitions is $9 - 9 = 0$.

**Lower bound.** The number of repetitions is always $\geq 0$ by definition (it counts excess occurrences). Since we have exhibited a configuration achieving 0, the minimum is exactly 0. $\blacksquare$
